newsitem.title: USA: US court grants order in Octel stock case.
newsitem.headline: US court grants order in Octel stock case.

text.p: A U.S. district court judge on Thursday issued a temporary restraining order against a software engineer at Octel Communications Corp and ordered his assets frozen after the Securities and Exchange Commission filed a complaint alleging he engaged in insider trading.

On Wednesday, the SEC said it filed a complaint against Shahryar Soroosh, alleging he engaged in insider trading in Octel stock. The commission said it had obtained an emergency order freezing his assets pending a hearing on Thursday.

On Wednesday, the SEC said it filed a complaint against Soroosh, alleging he engaged in illegal insider trading just before a company announcement last Thursday, which caused the price of Octel stock to drop more than 35 percent of its value the next day.
The commission alleged that Soroosh stood to profit by more than $500,000 through the alleged trades.
